# A component handed its fetch as a lambda, `fetch=func() => lookup(w)`,
# which its query calls through a lambda of its own,
# `fetch=func(k string) => fetch()`, under a `for`. The splice calls the
# caller's lambda where the query's stands, and neither literal carried the
# checker's async flag, so the query's fetch prop was typed as one that does
# not wait: Kotlin called a suspend function from a lambda that is not one.
#
# The fetch waits on the script harness's server.

sngl test --platform=none app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=fyne --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=bubbletea --language=go app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=html app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=android --language=kotlin app.sngl
stdout '1 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import async "sngl:async"
import http "sngl:http"
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

// The length of `name`, asked of the script harness's server.
func lookup(name string) async.Result[int] {
    match var r = http.get(url="http://127.0.0.1:47819/status/200") {
        failed { return {failed=r} }
        ok { return {ok=name.length()} }
    }
}

var lengths map[string, int] = {}

// Asks through the fetch its caller hands it.
component asker(key string, fetch func() async.Result[int]) ui.node {
    async.query(on=key, fetch=func(k string, life async.Lifetime) => fetch(), @load(got) { lengths[key] = got })
}

component many ui.node {
    ui.vbox {
        for var w = ["one", "three"] {
            asker(key=w, fetch=func() => lookup(w))
        }
    }
}

func testEachAnswerIsKept(t test.Test, c many) {
    t.setContext(http.answer, http.network)
    t.wait(func() => lengths.length() == 2, 5000)
    t.assert(lengths["three"] == 5)
}

ui.window {
    many()
}
